steps.surface: Message box → the mic button (desktop and Android)
steps.path: Any chat session → the mic beside Send; the first tap before the speech model is downloaded; a computer with no microphone; the Android message box; a remote browser tab; the card when the computer refuses microphone access; holding the space bar in an empty box
steps.headline: This is what done means.

rows.statement: Speech becomes text through Parakeet, downloaded once (464 MB) and running on your computer; your voice never leaves it.
rows.note: we may want to roadmap a fallback to built-in windows or mac speech services, but not rn

rows.statement: While you talk, everything since your last full stop stays grey; it turns solid when you finish a sentence.
One tap starts the mic; a second tap, Enter, the strip's Stop, or about two quiet seconds stops it.
rows.threshold: Silence stop after 2 s (measured on the deck)

rows.statement: After you stop, the text waits in the message box with the cursor at the end; nothing sends until you press Send.
The mic is in the message box from day one; before the model is downloaded, the first tap explains and offers the download.
On Android the mic uses the phone's own recognizer; words appear live in the app's box, ready to fix or send.
In a remote browser tab there is no mic button; voice ships on desktop and Android only.
rows.note: will need to note on roadmap though so we dont forget

rows.statement: The first tap opens a card above the mic: 'Speak your messages', with a one-time download of about 500 MB.
Download turns the card into a progress bar; when it finishes, a note says 'Voice is ready — tap the mic to talk.'
Not now closes the card and leaves the mic in place; nothing downloads without the Download tap.
With no microphone, the tap opens the card saying 'No microphone was found on this computer.' with one Check again button.
The reason on that card is always the one the computer reported, never a guess.
While you talk, a band above the box shows a green dot, 'Listening', the loudness bars, the clock and a Stop button.
rows.threshold: One 36 px band above the box (measured on the deck); the mic itself only glows

rows.statement: While listening, the ring around the mic grows with your loudness and sits still when you pause.
rows.threshold: Ring 2 to 9 px (measured on the deck); it moves only when the level changes

rows.statement: The mic sits between the message and Send, drawn like the paperclip; while it listens the placeholder reads 'Listening…'.
Typing while the mic is open ends dictation and keeps what you typed.
On Midnight and Dark the filled mic and its ring are the theme's light grey, not a colour.
In an empty box, holding the space bar a quarter second starts listening; letting go stops it; a quick tap does nothing.
rows.threshold: Listening starts after a 0.25 s hold (from the deck)

rows.statement: With any text in the box the space bar types a space as always; there is no other keyboard shortcut for the mic.
If refused, the card reads 'Microphone access was refused by your computer. Allow it for YouCoded in your system's privacy settings, then check again.'
That card has one Check again button; on a Mac the system's own permission prompt comes first, and the card appears only if declined.
The card names the language limit: it understands English and 24 other European languages.
While the download is being unpacked the card reads 'Almost ready…' with a bar that keeps moving.
